intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for data analysts on Mac. You hold a key, ask out loud, and it answers while it sees the sheet, chart or code on your screen. Most of an analyst's day goes to cleaning data, dealing with interruptions and rebuilding the same reports. This page shows where that time goes and which questions you can hand off.
tldr: Data analysts still spend much of the week on cleaning and manual preparation. IT Pro reports that three-quarters still rely on spreadsheets and manual prep.
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud, points at controls and walks you through steps.
Use it for the small questions: where a menu item lives, what an error means, and how to build a pivot one click at a time.
Follow your employer's rules on customer and company data before you show any of it to an AI tool.
Lazur does not click for you or edit your files. You still make the change and check the numbers.

blocks.text: Where a data analyst's day goes

Most research on work time looks at knowledge workers, not analysts. Treat the numbers here as the broad pattern, not your exact week. Still, the pattern holds. Your day splits between preparing data, answering questions and switching between apps.

Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index found the average knowledge worker received 117 emails a day. Most were skimmed in under 60 seconds. The same study counts an interruption every 2 minutes, or 275 a day, from meetings, emails or chats. That count uses the top 20% of users by ping volume, so it describes heavy users.

Asana's Anatomy of Work index, quoted in an April 2026 article, says 60% of time at work goes to 'work about work'. That covers status updates, coordination and chasing context. The same index puts duplicative work at 209 hours a year for the average knowledge worker. Copies of the source report the sample size differently, and the survey year is unclear, so use it as a rough signal.
Cleaning data is still most of the job

The clearest analyst number comes from IT Pro. It reports that three-quarters of data analysts still rely on spreadsheets and manual preparation. The article is dated 19 February 2025. It does not name the original study, the sample or the sponsor, so quote it as a press report.

Here is what that looks like on an ordinary morning. A sales export arrives with extra spaces after the region names. Some dates are stored as text. A few rows are duplicates. One column header changed name last month. Each fix takes a few minutes. Together they take the morning.

Microsoft's October 2026 post says Copilot in Excel's clean data skill is rolling out to general availability on Windows, Mac and web. It finds extra spaces, inconsistent formats, duplicates and wrong data types, then proposes fixes. Confirm your build has it before you plan a workflow around it.

blocks.title: Check your build first
blocks.text: Excel for Mac 16.114.3, dated 27 October 2026, is the latest release note entry I opened. Your build may be older or newer. Open Excel > About Excel to see yours.

What an AI assistant for data analysts should actually do

A useful assistant does four jobs while you work. It explains what you see. It points at the control you need. It guides you through a multi-step task. It drafts the words you send afterwards. Lazur covers those jobs. It does not do the work for you.

items: Explain: hold ⌥⌘ over an error, a formula or an odd-looking chart and ask what it means. Lazur answers out loud.
Point: ask where a menu item lives. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Guide: ask for steps. Lazur goes one click at a time and waits for each click before the next step.
Dictate and draft: hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor. Ask Lazur to draft a note, and it types the text for you to check.
Research and everyday: Lazur runs research in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. It also sets timers, Apple Reminders and Calendar events.

blocks.text: Memory helps too. Lazur keeps a record of what you asked and did, on your Mac. When you come back to a job on Thursday, the earlier question is still there.
Excel on Mac: shortcuts and version checks

Excel for Mac has its own shortcut set. Microsoft's support page lists ⌘⌥Return to insert a line break in a cell. It lists redo as ⌘Y or ⌘⇧Z. The Windows list has a Repeat entry that the Mac list does not. Third-party guides often show Repeat on Mac, so check the Edit menu before you rely on any list.

Version numbers matter too. Microsoft's release notes list Excel for Mac 16.114.3 as a quality and performance update. The September 2026 entry, 16.113, carried the Copilot in Excel changes. If a guide shows a button you cannot find, check your version first, then ask Lazur where it went.
Google Sheets on Mac in Chrome and Safari

Google Sheets runs in a browser, so your Mac is only the host. Several of our Sheets guides name Chrome in the title. Check your browser before you follow a steps list, since the steps may not match what you see.

For cleaning, start with Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates. The guide on [removing duplicate rows in Google Sheets](/how-to/remove-duplicate-rows-in-google-sheets) covers the options and what to check first. For category counts, the guide on [counting unique values](/how-to/count-unique-values-in-google-sheets) is a useful next step.
If most of your work sits in Sheets, the [Google Sheets page for data analysts](/for/data-analysts/google-sheets) walks through the common tasks in more detail.
Power BI and Tableau when you are on a Mac

Power BI Desktop is the hard case on a Mac. A Microsoft Learn Q&A answer from October 2024 says Power BI Desktop is not available for macOS. That answer came from a community member, not a Microsoft product page.

blocks.title: Confirm before you plan
blocks.text: Check Microsoft's current position on Power BI Desktop before you plan around it. The browser-based Power BI service needs a work or school account.

The routes that answer names take setup time. A Windows virtual machine through Parallels Desktop or Boot Camp is the usual suggestion. Lazur can point at Power BI controls on screen in the browser. It does not run Power BI for you.
Tableau is easier. Tableau Desktop 2024.2 and later runs natively on Apple silicon. Salesforce's help article says native operation needs macOS Ventura 13 or newer.
A worked example: cleaning one export by voice
Here is a realistic run. The file is open in Excel. One column header looks old, and you need to remove duplicate rows before you build the pivot.

items: Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what the odd header probably means. Lazur answers out loud from what it sees on screen.
Ask where Remove Duplicates lives. Lazur circles the menu item and labels it.
Ask Lazur to walk you through the dialog. It waits for each click, so you choose the columns that matter.
Count the rows before and after. Compare the total with your source system. Lazur cannot check your numbers against your database.
Hold fn and dictate a short note about what you removed. Lazur types it at the cursor for you to review.

blocks.text: The mistake is trusting the first answer. An assistant can tell you where a button is. It does not know your business rules. It also cannot judge rows you never showed it.
Privacy, company data and your employer's rules

Your employer sets the rules for company data, customer records and personal information. Follow those rules before you show or say any of that content to an AI tool. This page does not claim any compliance certification for Lazur. Lazur does not replace your company's data policy.

Here is how Lazur handles data. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

blocks.title: Close what you should not share
blocks.text: If the sheet shows customer names, contact details or other personal fields, close or mask those columns before you hold the key. Ask your data owner if you are unsure what the policy allows.
Mistakes people make with AI on data work

items: Asking for the answer, not the reason. Ask why a join drops rows, then verify the result yourself.
Holding the key with restricted data still on screen. Close the file first.
Accepting a summary of a report you have not read. Read the rows that drive the number.
Following a guide from a different Excel build. Check Excel > About Excel first.
Typing every note by hand. Hold fn and dictate, then spend the saved time on the analysis.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for data analysts?
faq.answer: It is an assistant that helps with the small questions that come up while you work. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. You hold ⌥⌘, ask out loud, and it answers while it sees your screen. It explains, points, guides and drafts. It does not click buttons or edit your files for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in Excel and Google Sheets on a Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur works with any app on your Mac that is on screen, including Excel and Google Sheets in a browser. It guides you through menus one click at a time. It does not operate those apps for you, and it is not an add-in for either one.

faq.question: Can Lazur build my pivot tables or run my cleaning steps?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides, points and drafts. You make the change in the file. That keeps you responsible for the result, which is where it belongs for a data analyst.

faq.question: Is my company data safe with it?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This page does not claim any compliance certification for your industry.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: How do I try it?
faq.answer: Download Lazur from the download page and start the Pro trial. The trial needs no credit card and starts when you first open the app. Check the pricing page for plans after that.

faq.question: Will it replace my BI tool?
faq.answer: No. Lazur helps with the questions around the tool. A Microsoft Learn Q&A answer says Power BI Desktop is not available on macOS, so Mac analysts often use the browser service or a Windows virtual machine.

faq.question: Can Lazur check my numbers?
faq.answer: No. It reads what is on your screen to answer you. It cannot check your figures against your source system. Compare totals and row counts yourself before you use them.

faq.question: Which shortcuts should I learn first?
faq.answer: Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Hold fn to dictate text at the cursor. Excel shortcut lists disagree on some Mac keys, so check the Edit menu before you rely on one.

faq.question: Is this only for analysts?
faq.answer: No. This page is written for analysts, but anyone who works in spreadsheets on a Mac can use the same shortcuts and the same steps.

painPoints.text: Microsoft's study of knowledge workers counts an interruption every 2 minutes. Each one costs you your place in a formula or a pivot. The study covers knowledge workers in general, not analysts.

painPoints.title: Work about work

painPoints.title: Menus that move
painPoints.text: Excel for Mac keeps shipping builds, such as 16.114.3 dated 27 October 2026. Guides go stale fast. You lose time when a step does not match the menu on your screen.
